invariant: Pre-L4 claim freeze is distinct from empirical Freeze A/B
required_semantics: PRE_L4_CLAIM_FREEZE_STATUS separate; FREEZE_LAYER only A/B

invariant: Only OUTCOME_DECISION_SCREEN uses SCREEN_STATUS/SCREEN_VERDICT
required_semantics: technical probe, measurement validation and formal study must not route through S15; a branch with OUTCOME_SCREEN_APPLICABILITY=NOT_APPLICABLE never acquires a screen verdict

invariant: Pre-outcome measurement validation precedes Death Pilot
required_semantics: S12 PASS before S13/S15

invariant: Formal main estimation/result QA precedes mechanism, robustness and writing
Risk-adaptive N/A never requires empty artifact
required_semantics: NOT_APPLICABLE means no empty ledger/template

invariant: Post-Pilot literature update is not result-driven redesign
required_semantics: effect sign/p-value/subgroup cannot drive collision search

invariant: Technical/data bugs use logs/tests/vendor docs before academic method literature
required_semantics: method literature escalates only for method-level uncertainty

invariant: RE alone recovers canonical project state and stops
required_semantics: No automatic research-state advance; structured state and registered artifacts first, archived conversation evidence only as needed.

invariant: AU alone audits and stops at the earliest material gap
required_semantics: No automatic research-state advance; distinguish research-state defects from presentation issues.

invariant: Canonical project-state module contains no concrete project/candidate IDs
required_semantics: project values live in project artifacts

invariant: Pre-L4 craft is diagnostic/optional, not an entry gate
required_semantics: argument architecture/one-paragraph test cannot block L4 by itself

invariant: Stable release requires validator PASS after final canonical edits
required_semantics: no ZIP publication on failed lint

invariant: No completion claim without closure PASS
required_semantics: Any claim of COMPLETE/PASS/next-step legality requires TASK_CLOSURE_STATUS=PASS.

invariant: Last result-affecting change invalidates prior validation
required_semantics: After any result/state-affecting edit, the final version must be revalidated before delivery.

invariant: Closure depth remains risk-adaptive
required_semantics: Ordinary tasks use LIGHT; MILESTONE validation is reserved for high-risk formal handoffs/results/releases.

invariant: Self-repair cannot hide blockers
required_semantics: Assistant-fixable defects are repaired before delivery; user-only dependencies remain BLOCKED and explicit.

invariant: Canonical fingerprint is recomputed, never trusted as declared
required_semantics: The validator recomputes CANONICAL_FINGERPRINT from the declared scope and fails on mismatch; a declared-but-unverifiable fingerprint is not acceptable evidence.

invariant: Generated runtime is verified independently of the builder
required_semantics: The validator re-derives generated content from the spec with its own parser; a tampered or stubbed builder cannot make a divergent generated file pass.

invariant: A package may not certify itself
required_semantics: RELEASE_METADATA.json carries identity only; validation, mutation, semantic-audit and closure verdicts live in release_evidence/ and in the detached attestation outside the ZIP.

invariant: Generated runtime is byte-identical across platforms
required_semantics: Generated files are written LF-only so that a rebuild on Windows does not invalidate manifest, checksums or fingerprint.

invariant: Documented validator capability equals implemented validator capability
required_semantics: Every check advertised in Index 8A maps to a named check emitted by tools/validate_skill.py.

invariant: Status values carry uniform, documented semantics
required_semantics: PASS/CONDITIONAL/BLOCKED/NOT_APPLICABLE mean the same thing across every status field; CONDITIONAL never satisfies a downstream gate that requires PASS and must carry a CONDITION_TYPE.

invariant: One milestone vocabulary
required_semantics: Closure depth, deliverable packaging and hash policy all reference the single registered MILESTONE_CLASS enum; no module maintains a parallel milestone list.

invariant: Freeze A checklist is derived from the state machine, not hand-maintained
required_semantics: Module 02 section 12 must cover every field named in S13 entry and pass_condition; a second hand-written gate definition is a drift source.

invariant: Every canonical rule is addressable and every gate reference resolves
required_semantics: Each rule-level heading in modules 01-07 carries a module-prefixed rule ID, and every GATE- token used in prose resolves to a registered gate_id.

invariant: A screen never establishes an economic null
required_semantics: OUTCOME_DECISION_SCREEN adjudicates resource allocation only; STOP_RESOURCE_ALLOCATION means the project is not worth further investment under the pre-frozen screening rule, never that the effect has been shown to be economically absent. Equivalence and minimum-effect conclusions belong to FORMAL_STUDY.

invariant: Screen data reuse is frozen before the effect is opened
required_semantics: SCREEN_DATA_REUSE_POLICY is recorded at S13, before B3. Default EXTERNAL_HOLDOUT. Reuse after the effect has been opened requires either a blinded nuisance-only argument, a valid adaptive or sequential procedure, or demotion of the formal result to exploratory.

invariant: The outcome screen is optional
required_semantics: When a holdout would destroy formal power, OUTCOME_SCREEN_APPLICABILITY=NOT_APPLICABLE and the branch proceeds from S13 to S17 without opening any effect.

invariant: Multiplicity is governed in three separate layers
required_semantics: Within-study multiplicity, specification search on one dataset, and literature-level selection are distinct problems with distinct remedies; a within-study correction never discharges the other two.

invariant: Every terminated branch has a terminal state
required_semantics: All formal STOP and STOP_RESOURCE_ALLOCATION paths route to S24, which records termination reason, failure class, reusable assets, cooldown/reopen conditions, and Seen Data status. No transition targets a bare terminal word without an archive record.

invariant: Blinding is a principle, not an event-study template
required_semantics: The firewall hides the current study's answer while analysis choices remain discretionary; each design maps it via BLINDING_IMPLEMENTATION_MODE. Background familiarity with a standard dataset is not an unblinding event.

invariant: External method precedent carries an explicit transfer status
required_semantics: Every canonical rule resting on outside methodological authority appears in the method source locator registry with a locator and a PRECEDENT_TRANSFER_STATUS, including what the source does not support.

invariant: Previously created or acquired project assets are resolved before re-upload is requested
required_semantics: When a task depends on a prior artifact not directly attached, search the current workspace and registered project assets, verify candidate identity/version, and request user re-upload only after no usable copy is found or host access is blocked.

invariant: A recorded verification is reusable until an invalidation trigger fires
required_semantics: Re-verification of a prior asset is triggered by change, not by the arrival of a new task. The data asset schema carries verified_at, verified_hash, verification_scope and verification_result so the result has somewhere to live, and PRIOR_ASSET_RESOLUTION routes through the reuse rule instead of re-checking unconditionally.

invariant: Estimation output requires a resolved empirical entry
required_semantics: No coefficient, test statistic, portfolio return or model performance number is produced before the current pipeline state is anchored and the upstream data states are evidenced. GATE-STATE-NOSKIP carries an executable entry procedure rather than a silent posture, and the absence of a user request is never a reason to skip a state.

invariant: Every rule leaning on outside authority is registered or points at the registry
required_semantics: A module rule that cites an external author, guideline or standard either has its own row in the method source locator registry or explicitly references that registry. The registry check runs in both directions, so a source cannot be used as authority in prose while being absent from the registry.

invariant: An always-on gate names an executable procedure, not a silence posture
required_semantics: Every gate with activation_class ALWAYS_ON states what it actually does and names at least one rule that carries the procedure. A gate whose execution is only a declaration of silence has no way to detect the condition it guards and is indistinguishable at runtime from an absent gate.

invariant: Adverse evidence is held to the tier that would be needed to establish the claim
required_semantics: A contribution may not be stopped or narrowed by a source weaker than one that could have established the same proposition. The tier of the adverse source is recorded, and a source below the supporting tier can at most defer the verdict, never close it. Absence of a search hit is search-process evidence and never establishes novelty or collision.

invariant: An irreversible action stays done after a later failure
required_semantics: Warnings, recoverable failures and irreversible external state changes are distinguished. Once a result has been opened, an external job submitted, funds committed or a message sent, a subsequent error does not undo it and may not be reported as if the action had not occurred.

invariant: Every rule is locatable without reading its whole module
required_semantics: A generated locator index maps every rule id to its module and section, and the loader routes through it. Locating one rule must not require loading a 25k-token module, because in a chat session every module read is spent permanently from the same context the work itself needs.

invariant: Cross-module concepts have exactly one canonical definition
required_semantics: Evidence hierarchy, Seen Data schema and the empirical execution taxonomy are each stated once; other modules reference rather than restate them.
